| `GET /api/admin/users/:id`                             | Admin                   | One account with activity counts and recent role and status history.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `PATCH /api/admin/users/:id/role`                      | Admin                   | Body`{ role, reason }`.`role`is`USER`,`MODERATOR`or`ADMIN`. Not your own role; the person needs an active account with a confirmed email to become staff.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `POST /api/admin/users/:id/suspend`                    | Admin                   | Body`{ reason }`. Not yourself. The person is locked out from their next request and is told the reason.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `POST /api/admin/users/:id/reactivate`                 | Admin                   | Lifts a suspension.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `POST /api/moderation/hospitals/:id/suspend`           | Admin only              | Body`{ "reason": "…" }`. Blocks claims, verification and link edits.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `POST /api/moderation/hospitals/:id/unsuspend`         | Admin only              | The status is worked out again from the hospital's history, so a verified hospital comes back verified.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `POST /api/auth/register`                              | none                    | Limited to 10/hour per IP. Same response for new and existing emails.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `POST /api/auth/login`                                 | none                    | 5 failed attempts per 15 min per IP + email.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `POST /api/auth/forgot-password`                       | none                    | 3/hour per email address. Always answers 200.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `POST /api/auth/resend-confirmation`                   | none                    | 3/hour per email address. Always answers 200.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `POST /api/auth/logout`                                | Bearer                  | Body:`{ "refreshToken": "…" }`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `GET /api/auth/me`                                     | Bearer                  | Returns the signed-in user.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `GET /api/users/me`                                    | Bearer                  | Full profile: name, username, avatar, phone, language, timezone, theme and more.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `PATCH /api/users/me`                                  | Bearer                  | Update any of those fields (send only what changes;`null`clears name, username, phone and avatar). 30 changes per 15 min per user.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `GET /api/users/me/notification-preferences`           | Bearer                  | Returns the settings, creating defaults on first use.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `PATCH /api/users/me/notification-preferences`         | Bearer                  | Update notification switches. Security alerts can't be turned off.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

All error responses look like: `{ "success": false, "message": "…", "code": "…", "requestId": "…", "errors": [{ "field", "message" }] }` (`errors` appears only for validation failures).

### Database rules the API relies on

These are CHECK constraints on the `hospitals` table in Supabase (they do not appear in the migration files):


| Column                | Allowed values                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ownership`           | `federal`,`state`,`private`                                                                                                                                         |
| `verification_status` | `unclaimed`,`claim_pending`,`claimed`,`verification_pending`,`verified`,`rejected`,`suspended`(the workflow for claiming and verifying a hospital, used in task 6c) |
| `year_established`    | empty, or between 1000 and 9999                                                                                                                                     |

Public responses show `status` as only `verified`, `claimed` or `unclaimed`. Rejected claims and suspensions are never shown publicly; the full seven values are for the claimant and admins (task 6c).

Rules added by the reviews migration (task 6b):


| Table and column                                 | Rule                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `reviews.overall_rating`,`review_ratings.rating` | 1 to 5                                                                                                           |
| `reviews.status`                                 | `pending_moderation`,`published`,`rejected`,`removed`(`removed`is reserved for the moderation work in task 6d)   |
| `reviews.title`,`reviews.comment`                | 3-150 and 20-5000 characters                                                                                     |
| `reviews.published_at`                           | set exactly when the status is`published`                                                                        |
| `reviews (user_id, hospital_id)`                 | unique: one review per user per hospital.`user_id`becomes empty when an account is deleted, and the review stays |
| `review_ratings (review_id, category)`           | unique, and the category must be one of the eight names above                                                    |

### How reviews work

* **Lifecycle:** a new review is `pending_moderation`. A moderator approves it (`published`) or rejects it with a reason (`rejected`). An author can edit a rejected review, which sends it back to `pending_moderation`. Setting `REVIEWS_REQUIRE_MODERATION=false` publishes reviews immediately (useful while testing).
* **Editing:** changing the title, comment, overall rating, category ratings or department re-queues the review, and while it waits it is hidden and not counted. Changing only `isAnonymous` or the visit date does not.
* **Ratings:** a hospital's average counts published reviews only. Database triggers keep `hospital_rating_stats` correct however a review changes (API, SQL editor, deletion), and they serialize overlapping updates per hospital. `ranking_score` is a damped average, `(count × average + 5 × 3.5) ÷ (count + 5)`, and is 0 for hospitals without reviews, which is what `sort=rating` uses.
* **Privacy:** anonymous reviews, and reviews whose author deleted their account, show "Anonymous". Moderators can still see who wrote a review, so abuse can be dealt with. The audit log records review ids, never review text.
* **Who moderates:** accounts with the role `MODERATOR` or `ADMIN`. Administrators give and take these roles through the API (see "Roles and account management"); the first administrator is made with `npm run make:admin -- you@example.com`. A role change applies on the person's next request.
* **Reviews are plain text.** Links are refused, but the frontend must still show them as text, never as HTML.

### Claims, verification and hospital status

A hospital's internal status (`hospitals.verification_status`) moves like this:


| From                   | Event                                    | To                                                                                |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unclaimed`,`rejected` | someone submits a claim                  | `claim_pending`                                                                   |
| `claim_pending`        | a moderator approves a claim             | `claimed`(the claimant becomes a representative; other waiting claims are closed) |
| `claim_pending`        | the last waiting claim is rejected       | `rejected`(can be claimed again)                                                  |
| `claim_pending`        | the last waiting claim is withdrawn      | `unclaimed`                                                                       |
| `claimed`              | the representative asks for verification | `verification_pending`                                                            |
| `verification_pending` | a moderator approves                     | `verified`                                                                        |
| `verification_pending` | a moderator rejects                      | `claimed`(the representative can submit again)                                    |
| anything               | an admin suspends                        | `suspended`(an admin restores it; the status is worked out again)                 |

* **Several people can claim the same hospital at once.** A moderator decides between them. One person can have 3 claims waiting and submit 5 per day.
* **Verification** needs the written details (registration body, registration number, optional official email) AND at least one uploaded document before a moderator can approve it (`REQUIRE_DOCUMENT_FOR_VERIFICATION` at the top of `claimModeration.controller.js`). Claims can carry documents too (for example a letter of authority), but they are optional there.
* **Representatives** are the people with an approved claim (table `hospital_staff`). Authority is per hospital; no global role is changed.
* **Conflict of interest:** a representative, and anyone with a claim waiting, cannot review that hospital (403 `CONFLICT_OF_INTEREST`), including editing a review they wrote earlier. A review written before they became a representative stays published; moderators can remove it.
* **Social links** are typed in by representatives only (6 platforms, checked by `src/utils/socialLinks.js`) and shown publicly while the hospital is `claimed`, `verification_pending` or `verified`. They are stored in `hospitals.social_media`, never in the imported `hospital_data`.
* **Suspended hospitals** still appear in the directory (shown as `unclaimed`) but cannot be claimed, verified or edited.
* **Concurrency:** every transaction that changes claims or status locks the hospital row first (`lockHospital`). Without this, two moderators approving rival claims at the same moment deadlocked in testing.

### Roles and account management

Three roles can be given to a person:


| Role        | What they can do                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `USER`      | An ordinary member: write reviews, report reviews, claim a hospital.                                                                                                                            |
| `MODERATOR` | Everything above, plus the moderation tools: the review, claim, verification, report and response queues, and reading the moderation history. They cannot manage accounts or suspend hospitals. |
| `ADMIN`     | Everything a moderator can do, plus suspending and restoring hospitals, and managing accounts and roles (below).                                                                                |

`HOSPITAL_REP` and `SUPPORT` exist in the database but are never assigned. A hospital representative's authority belongs to one hospital (an approved claim), not to a global role, and `SUPPORT` has no permissions defined yet. Someone who already holds one can be set back to `USER`.

**The first administrator, without SQL.** After the person has signed up and confirmed their email:

```
npm run make:admin -- you@example.com
```

It refuses to run once an active administrator exists (add `--force` only if you really must, for example if every administrator account was lost), and it is recorded in the moderation history as "Command line". From then on, administrators manage roles through the API.


| Endpoint (admins only)                 | What it does                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /api/admin/users`                 | Find accounts.`?q=`matches part of the email, display name or username;`?role=MODERATOR`lists the moderators;`?status=active`or`suspended`;`page`,`limit`. |
| `GET /api/admin/users/:id`             | One account with its activity counts (reviews and claims by status), the hospitals it represents, and its recent role and status history.                  |
| `PATCH /api/admin/users/:id/role`      | Body`{ "role": "MODERATOR", "reason": "..." }`. The reason is required, recorded, and told to the person. Takes effect on their next request.              |
| `POST /api/admin/users/:id/suspend`    | Body`{ "reason": "..." }`. The person is locked out from their next request and is told the reason.                                                        |
| `POST /api/admin/users/:id/reactivate` | Lifts a suspension. The person is told.                                                                                                                    |

What an admin sees of a person is what is needed to manage the account: email, name, role, status, and counts. Never phone numbers, saved locations or notification settings. Moderators cannot use any of these endpoints.

Safeguards:

* **Nobody changes or suspends their own account**, so an administrator cannot lock themselves out or keep a role they should lose.
* **MODERATOR and ADMIN go only to active accounts with a confirmed email.**
* **Every change needs a reason**, is written to the moderation history inside the same transaction (target type `user`; actions `user.role_change`, `user.suspend`, `user.reactivate`), and is told to the person. These notices (`account.role_changed`, `account.suspended`, `account.reactivated`) are always sent, in the app and by email, whatever the person's notification settings, and even to a suspended account.
* **The last active administrator can never be demoted, suspended or deleted.** Two layers: (1) every change first locks all active admin rows and checks that the person making it is still an active admin, so two administrators demoting each other at the same instant cannot leave none (the second is refused with 403 `NOT_AN_ADMIN`); (2) a database trigger (`users_protect_last_admin`) refuses the same thing for any other route, such as the Supabase table editor or a SQL statement, and uses a lock so two simultaneous SQL attempts also queue up. Both were tested, including the simultaneous cases.
* **Suspension takes effect at once.** Sign-in and every API request check the account, and the role is read from the database on every request, so there are no stale tokens. If `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is set, Supabase is also told to stop issuing tokens to the person (best effort: if Supabase cannot be reached the suspension still stands, and the response says `signInBlocked: false`).
* **A suspension does not touch the person's content.** Their published reviews stay visible; moderators handle content through the usual tools.

Not built: a person cannot appeal a suspension, there is no bulk action, and an administrator cannot edit another person's profile (name, email, phone).

### Reports, responses and moderation history

**Reporting a review.** Anyone signed in with a confirmed email can report a published review (`POST /api/reviews/:id/reports`) with a reason (`spam`, `abusive_language`, `fake_review`, `conflict_of_interest`, `privacy_violation`, `irrelevant`, `other`) and optional details. A hospital's own representatives can report too; moderators see that flag. Limits: one report per person per review, not your own review, 10 reports a day.

**Policy: a report never hides a review by itself.** However many arrive, the review stays published and keeps counting toward the hospital's rating until a moderator decides. Otherwise a hospital, or a group of friends, could remove honest criticism just by reporting it. The same applies while a case is "under investigation".

How moderators work reports (one decision per review, not per report):


| Step            | Endpoint                                                           | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| See the queue   | `GET /api/moderation/reports`                                      | One entry per reported review, escalated cases first, then oldest first, with reasons counted and every report (reporters shown by name, never email).`?status=open`(default),`investigating`,`upheld`,`dismissed`;`?escalated=true`. |
| Look into it    | `POST /api/moderation/reviews/:id/reports/investigate`             | Open reports become`investigating`. Review stays published.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Pass it up      | `POST /api/moderation/reviews/:id/reports/escalate`(note required) | Only an administrator can then dismiss or uphold the case (403`ESCALATED_TO_ADMIN`otherwise).                                                                                                                                         |
| Keep the review | `POST /api/moderation/reviews/:id/reports/dismiss`                 | Reports become`dismissed`; the reporters are told. The review's author is not told anything.                                                                                                                                          |
| Take it down    | `POST /api/moderation/reviews/:id/reports/uphold`(reason required) | The review is rejected (same takedown as the review queue), its author is told with the reason, and the reporters are told it was removed.                                                                                            |

Moderators cannot decide reports about their own review. Two moderators acting at once: exactly one decision wins. After a decision the same review can be reported again by someone who has not reported it yet.

**Hospital responses.** A representative of a hospital can reply publicly to a published review: `PUT /api/reviews/:id/response` (create or replace), `DELETE` to remove it, and `GET /api/hospitals/:id/responses?unanswered=true` for a dashboard of the hospital's reviews with their response status (a rejected response shows the moderator's note). Rules:

* one response per review, 10 to 1500 characters, no links;
* only to a published review, only while the hospital has a representative and is not suspended, and never to a review the representative wrote themselves;
* a moderator approves each response before it appears (`GET /api/moderation/responses`, then `approve` or `reject` with a reason). Editing a response, even a published one, sends it back to moderation. Set `RESPONSES_REQUIRE_MODERATION=false` to publish responses at once;
* the public review shows `response: { body, respondedAt }` once published (otherwise `null`). It never shows who wrote it;
* a response cannot change a review or the rating, and representatives have no way to delete or hide a review;
* the reviewer is told when a reply appears (their `hospitalResponses` setting), and the representative is told when it is approved or rejected.

**Moderation history.**`GET /api/moderation/history` lists every action a moderator or admin has taken, newest first: `review.approve`, `review.reject`, `report.investigate`, `report.escalate`, `report.dismiss`, `report.uphold`, `response.approve`, `response.reject`, `claim.approve`, `claim.reject`, `verification.approve`, `verification.reject`, `hospital.suspend`, `hospital.restore`, `user.role_change`, `user.suspend` and `user.reactivate`. Filter with `targetType` (`review`, `response`, `claim`, `verification`, `hospital`, `user`) plus `targetId` for everything that ever happened to one item, `actorId` for everything one person did, and `action`. Each entry has the actor's name and role, the reason given, and the time; never an email address.

* It is written **inside the same database transaction as the action**, so there is never a decision without a record, and if the record cannot be written the decision is cancelled (tested by breaking the log on purpose).
* It is **append-only**: a database trigger refuses any change or delete, even by the application. The table has no foreign keys and copies the actor's name, so the record survives deleted accounts and reviews. It is never pruned.
* It records decisions made from the day this task was installed; earlier decisions are not back-filled (their reasons are still on the rows themselves).

Not built: moderators cannot be notified of new reports, there is no appeal for a reviewer whose review was taken down, and a reporter cannot see the status of their own reports (they are told the outcome).

### Notifications and email

Things that happen to a person produce an in-app notification (`GET /api/notifications`) and, if they allow it, an email. The email is **queued** first and sent a moment later by a background worker, so a slow, broken or not-yet-configured mail server never makes a moderator's decision fail or wait.


| What happens                                                                 | Who is told                                                                             | Type                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| A claim is submitted                                                         | the claimant                                                                            | `claim.submitted`                                |
| A claim is approved                                                          | the claimant                                                                            | `claim.approved`                                 |
| A claim is rejected (with the moderator's reason)                            | the claimant                                                                            | `claim.rejected`                                 |
| Another claim for the same hospital is approved                              | the other claimants                                                                     | `claim.superseded`                               |
| A verification request is submitted, approved, or rejected (with the reason) | the requester                                                                           | `verification.submitted`,`.approved`,`.rejected` |
| An admin suspends or restores a hospital                                     | the hospital's representatives (the admin's internal reason is never included)          | `hospital.suspended`,`hospital.restored`         |
| A review is published, or rejected (with the reason)                         | the author, even if the review is anonymous                                             | `review.published`,`review.rejected`             |
| A hospital's response to your review appears                                 | the reviewer                                                                            | `response.received`                              |
| A hospital response is approved or rejected (with the reason)                | the representative who wrote it                                                         | `response.approved`,`response.rejected`          |
| A report you made is decided                                                 | the reporter (upheld: "the review was removed"; dismissed: "it follows the guidelines") | `report.upheld`,`report.dismissed`               |

Each person's settings (`notification_preferences`, set with `PATCH /api/users/me`) decide what they get: `claimUpdates` or `reviewUpdates` off means nothing at all of that kind; `inAppNotifications` off means no in-app message; `emailNotifications` off means no email. Someone with no settings row gets everything. `hospitalResponses` controls "a hospital replied to my review"; the two messages a representative gets about their own response follow `claimUpdates`, and report outcomes follow `reviewUpdates`.

How the queue behaves:


| Situation                                                                | What happens                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Email not set up (`SMTP_HOST`empty)                                      | Emails wait in the queue; a warning is printed once. Nothing is lost.                                                             |
| `MAIL_MODE=log`                                                          | The email is printed in the server console and marked sent. For development.                                                      |
| Mail server down or slow                                                 | Retried after 1, 5, 30 and 120 minutes; given up after 5 tries (status`failed`).                                                  |
| Wrong SMTP login                                                         | Treated as a setup problem, not the email's fault: a loud message, retried every 15 minutes without using up the email's tries.   |
| Server says the address can never work (for example 550 no such mailbox) | Marked`failed`at once.                                                                                                            |
| An email is more than 72 hours old                                       | Dropped (`expired`): a late "your claim was received" only confuses.                                                              |
| Server crashed mid-send                                                  | The email is put back after 10 minutes.                                                                                           |
| Several workers at once                                                  | Each takes its own emails (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), so none is sent twice.                                                      |
| Old records                                                              | Sent emails are deleted after 30 days, failed ones after 90, read notifications after 90 days, and any notification after a year. |

Safeguards: all text that came from a person (hospital names, moderators' reasons) is HTML-escaped; subjects are forced onto one line so a name cannot inject email headers; links are built only from `FRONTEND_URL` and fixed paths; mail is marked automatic so mail programs do not auto-reply; the SMTP login is refused if it cannot be encrypted.

**Going live checklist** (after you buy the domain):

1. Create a mailbox or SMTP account for `noreply@yourdomain` with a mail provider (a transactional email service, or a mailbox host that offers SMTP). Your provider's documentation lists the SMTP host, port and whether to use an app password or an SMTP key.
2. Add the DNS records your provider asks for to prove the domain is yours and to sign your mail: usually SPF and DKIM, and a DMARC record. Without them, many inboxes (Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook) will send your emails to spam or refuse them.
3. Fill in `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` and `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS` in `.env`, and remove `MAIL_MODE=log` (or set `MAIL_MODE=smtp`). See `.env.example`.
4. Run `npm run test:email -- you@example.com`. It checks the connection and login, sends a test, and says what is wrong in plain language if not.
5. Restart the server. The queue's waiting emails go out (anything older than 72 hours is dropped).
6. If your host puts the server to sleep, set `MAIL_WORKER=off` and run `npm run send:emails` every few minutes from a scheduler instead.

Not built: push notifications (the `pushNotifications` setting is saved but unused), bounce handling and delivery tracking, an unsubscribe link (people change what they receive in their notification settings, which every email links to), and emails to moderators about new claims waiting.

### Proof documents (uploads)

Representatives and claimants attach proof (a CAC certificate, an operating licence, a letter of authority, a staff ID). The files live in a **private** Supabase Storage bucket, never in the database and never passing through this server.

How an upload works:

1. **Ask for a link:**`POST /api/claims/:id/documents` (or `/verifications/:id/documents`) with the document type, file name, file type and size. The server records the file as `awaiting_upload` and returns `upload: { bucket, path, token, ... }`.
2. **Upload from the browser** straight to Supabase: `supabase.storage.from(upload.bucket).uploadToSignedUrl(upload.path, upload.token, file, { contentType })`. The link works for one file at exactly that path.
3. **Confirm:**`POST /api/documents/:id/confirm`. The server reads the real file: its size and its first bytes. A file that is empty, over 5 MB, or not a genuine PDF/JPEG/PNG of the declared type (for example a program renamed `licence.pdf`) is **deleted** and refused with 422.

Rules and safeguards:


| Rule                  | Detail                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Allowed files         | PDF, JPEG and PNG, up to 5 MB, at most 5 per claim or request. The bucket enforces the same limits independently.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Storage path          | Built only from ids and a fixed extension (`claims/<claimId>/<documentId>.pdf`). The user's file name is shown but never used in a path. The path is never sent to any client.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Who can add or delete | Only the person who made the claim or request, and only while it is waiting for review.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Who can open files    | Moderators and admins only, through a link that lasts 5 minutes. Each link is written to the audit log (`HOSPITAL_DOCUMENT_VIEWED`) before it exists; if the log cannot be written, no link is given.                                                                                                                            |
| Retention             | When a claim or request is decided (approved, rejected or withdrawn) its files are scheduled for deletion 30 days later (`RETENTION_DAYS_AFTER_DECISION`in`src/utils/documents.js`).`npm run purge:documents`does the deleting; rows stay as a record, marked`purged`. Uploads nobody confirmed within 24 hours are removed too. |
| Not set up yet        | Without`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`the app still runs; only the document routes answer 503`DOCUMENTS_UNAVAILABLE`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

What is NOT covered: files of a hospital deleted outright are not removed from storage automatically (hospitals are not deleted in normal use), and there is no virus scanning of uploads. The type check stops disguised programs but does not detect malicious PDFs; moderators should open files with normal care.

### Hospital response shape

Names and nesting follow the approved shape, written in camelCase. Values come straight from the database columns, so nothing is converted just to match the sample. `GET /api/hospitals/:id` returns everything below. List items (`GET /api/hospitals`) carry the same `id`, `hospitalName`, `location`, `status` and `rating`, plus `type`, `ownership` and `distanceKm` (near-me searches only), but no `contact`, `services` or `info`.

```json
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "hospitalName": "Name of the hospital",
  "location": {
    "state": { "id": 24, "name": "Lagos" },
    "city": "Yaba",
    "lga": { "id": 900, "name": "Lagos Mainland" },
    "address": "1 Herbert Macaulay Way",
    "coordinates": { "lat": 6.51, "lon": 3.38 }
  },
  "contact": {
    "phoneNumber": ["+2348031234567"],
    "email": ["info@example.ng"],
    "website": "https://example.ng",
    "socialMedia": { "facebook": "https://facebook.com/example" }
  },
  "services": ["Laboratory", "Maternity", "Surgery"],
  "info": {
    "hours": "08:00 - 23:00",
    "facilities": ["Ambulance", "Pharmacy", "Theatre"],
    "insurance": ["NHIA"],
    "accreditation": ["MDCN"]
  },
  "status": "unclaimed | claimed | verified",
  "rating": { "average": 4.25, "count": 12 },
  "type": { "id": 1, "name": "General Hospital" },
  "ownership": "private",
  "description": null,
  "yearEstablished": null,
  "accessibilityInformation": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-11-23T20:51:04.946Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-11-23T20:51:04.946Z"
}
```

Where this differs from the approved sample, on purpose:


| Field                                 | Approved sample | What the API returns                        | Why                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `location.lga`                        | string          | `{ id, name }`                              | Matches`location.state`and works with the`lgaId`filter.                                                                                                           |
| `contact.phoneNumber`,`contact.email` | single string   | array of strings                            | A hospital can have several, and the imported data already holds lists. The names stay singular to match the sample.                                              |
| `info.insurance`,`info.accreditation` | string          | array of strings                            | Same reason.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `status`                              | seven values    | `unclaimed`,`claimed`or`verified`           | Rejections and suspensions are not shown publicly.                                                                                                                |
| `rating`                              | one number      | `{ average, count }`                        | A 4.8 from one review must not look like a 4.8 from 400.`average`is`null`with no reviews.                                                                         |
| `contact.socialMedia`                 | object          | `{}`or`{ platform: url }`                   | Imported links were wrong. Only links typed in by a hospital's own representatives are shown, and only while the hospital is claimed or verified. Always present. |
| `location.coordinates`                | object          | `null`when latitude or longitude is missing |                                                                                                                                                                   |

Cleaning rules: facilities are sorted A-Z (case-insensitive); other lists keep their original order. Every list drops placeholders ("unknown", "TBD"), markup and duplicates, and holds at most 30 items.

### What `hospital_data` holds and what the public sees

`hospitals.hospital_data` is imported, unvetted JSON. In the one sample checked (University College Hospital, Ibadan) it contained spam image links on what looks like a hijacked subdomain (gambling-site file names), social-media links belonging to an unrelated company, and placeholders such as "TBD - TBD" and "unknown". It is therefore never sent as it is.


| Part of`hospital_data`                                                                     | Shown publicly?                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `contact.website`                                                                          | Yes, if it is a valid http(s) address without embedded passwords                                             |
| `contact.phone_number`,`contact.email`                                                     | Yes, if valid; phone numbers are converted to`+234…`format                                                  |
| `info.hours`,`info.insurance`,`info.facilities`,`info.accreditation`,`services`            | Yes, as clean plain text: placeholders, markup and duplicates removed, at most 30 items, 100 characters each |
| `images`(hero image, icon)                                                                 | **No**: spam risk                                                                                            |
| `contact.social_media`                                                                     | **No**: wrong accounts were found                                                                            |
| everything else (`location`,`ownership`,`hospital_type`,`verification_status`, other keys) | No: the real table columns are used instead                                                                  |

Audit queries to run in the Supabase SQL editor (read-only):

```sql
-- Which hosts do hero images come from?
select coalesce(substring(hospital_data->'images'->>'hero_image' from '^https?://([^/]+)'), '(none)') as host, count(*)
from hospitals group by 1 order by 2 desc limit 20;

-- Anything that looks like gambling spam?
select id, hospital_name, hospital_data->'images' as images, hospital_data->'contact'->>'website' as website
from hospitals where hospital_data::text ~* '(toto|slot|gacor|togel|judi|casino|poker)' limit 50;

-- Is the TeePublic social link a bulk default?
select hospital_data->'contact'->'social_media'->>'twitter' as twitter, count(*)
from hospitals group by 1 order by 2 desc limit 5;
```

If any frontend code reads `hospital_data` straight from Supabase instead of through this API, it will show the unfiltered data.

## 6. Environment variables (`.env`)


| Variable                              | Needed                    | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DATABASE_URL`                        | yes                       | Postgres connection string used by the app (Supabase transaction pooler, port 6543).**Must include`pgbouncer=true`**, for example`...:6543/postgres?pgbouncer=true&connect_timeout=60`. Without it Prisma's engine fails with "prepared statement already exists" errors. |
| `DIRECT_URL`                          | yes (Prisma 6)            | Session-pooler or direct connection (port 5432) used only by Prisma CLI commands such as`prisma db pull`. Declared as`directUrl`in`schema.prisma`.                                                                                                                        |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`           | yes, for document uploads | Supabase dashboard, Project settings, API keys, the`service_role`key.**It can do anything in your project.**Keep it in`.env`on the server only; never put it in the frontend, in git, or in a chat.                                                                       |
| `DOCUMENT_BUCKET`                     | no                        | Name of the private bucket. Defaults to`verification-documents`, which`prisma/supabase-storage-bucket.sql`creates.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `FRONTEND_URL`                        | yes                       | The website's address. Also used to build the links in emails (the first address is used if you list several).                                                                                                                                                            |
| `MAIL_MODE`                           | no                        | `smtp`(default): send through the SMTP server.`log`: print emails in the server console instead of sending (use it until the domain and mailbox exist).`off`: send nothing; emails wait in the queue.                                                                     |
| `SMTP_HOST`,`SMTP_PORT`,`SMTP_SECURE` | for smtp mode             | Your mail provider's SMTP server. Port 587 with`SMTP_SECURE`unset is the usual choice; use 465 with`SMTP_SECURE=true`if your provider says so. While`SMTP_HOST`is empty, emails wait in the queue.                                                                        |
| `SMTP_USER`,`SMTP_PASSWORD`           | for smtp mode             | The mailbox login (often the full address) and its password or the provider's SMTP key. Keep the password only in`.env`.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `SMTP_REQUIRE_TLS`                    | no                        | `true`by default: the login is never sent unencrypted. Set`false`only for a local test mail server.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`,`MAIL_FROM_NAME`  | no                        | The sender. Defaults:`noreply@hospitalreviewplatform.com`and the app name. The address must belong to a domain you have verified with your provider.                                                                                                                      |
| `MAIL_REPLY_TO`,`SUPPORT_EMAIL`       | no                        | Where replies go, and the address shown in the suspension email.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `APP_NAME`                            | no                        | Shown in emails. Default`Dreel`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `MAIL_WORKER`                         | no                        | Set to`off`to stop the server sending queued emails itself (when you run`npm run send:emails`from a scheduler instead).                                                                                                                                                   |
| `RESPONSES_REQUIRE_MODERATION`        | no                        | Hospital responses wait for a moderator unless this is`false`.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `SUPABASE_URL`,`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`    | yes                       | Supabase project and public key.`SUPABASE_URL`is also used to check that avatar URLs point at this project's storage.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `PASSWORD_RESET_REDIRECT_URL`         | yes                       | Where the password-reset email link sends the user.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `FRONTEND_URL`                        | recommended               | Frontend address: redirect after email confirmation, and CORS fallback.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `CORS_ORIGINS`                        | production                | Comma-separated frontend origins allowed to call the API.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `TRUST_PROXY`                         | when behind a proxy       | Number of proxy hops (usually`1`), so rate limits and audit logs see real client IPs. Leave unset locally.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ENABLE_API_DOCS`                     | optional                  | `true`to expose`/api-docs`in production.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `PORT`                                | optional                  | Defaults to 5000.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `NODE_ENV`                            | production                | Set to`production`when deployed (hides debug detail, tightens CORS and docs).                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `REVIEWS_REQUIRE_MODERATION`          | optional                  | `false`publishes new and edited reviews immediately. Anything else, or unset, holds them for a moderator.                                                                                                                                                                 |

## 7. Audit events (table `security_events`)

Each row stores `metadata` with `requestId`, `ip` and `userAgent` (plus extras). Events: `ACCOUNT_REGISTERED`, `REGISTRATION_DUPLICATE_EMAIL`, `LOGIN_SUCCESSFUL`, `LOGIN_FAILED`, `LOGIN_BLOCKED_DEACTIVATED`, `LOGOUT`, `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED`, `CONFIRMATION_EMAIL_REQUESTED`, `PROFILE_UPDATED` and `NOTIFICATION_PREFERENCES_UPDATED` (these two list the changed field names only), `REVIEW_CREATED`, `REVIEW_UPDATED`, `REVIEW_DELETED`, `REVIEW_APPROVED` and `REVIEW_REJECTED` (review and hospital ids only; the text and the moderator's reason are never logged), `HOSPITAL_CLAIM_SUBMITTED`, `HOSPITAL_CLAIM_WITHDRAWN`, `HOSPITAL_CLAIM_APPROVED`, `HOSPITAL_CLAIM_REJECTED`, `HOSPITAL_VERIFICATION_REQUESTED`, `HOSPITAL_VERIFICATION_APPROVED`, `HOSPITAL_VERIFICATION_REJECTED`, `HOSPITAL_SOCIAL_MEDIA_UPDATED` (platform names only), `HOSPITAL_SUSPENDED` (with the admin's reason), `HOSPITAL_RESTORED`, `HOSPITAL_DOCUMENT_UPLOADED`, `HOSPITAL_DOCUMENT_DELETED` and `HOSPITAL_DOCUMENT_VIEWED` (who opened which document; the file name and contents are never logged), `REVIEW_REPORTED` (reason only, never the details), `REVIEW_REPORT_ESCALATED`, `REVIEW_REPORTS_DISMISSED`, `REVIEW_REPORTS_UPHELD`, `REVIEW_RESPONSE_CREATED`, `_UPDATED`, `_DELETED`, `_APPROVED` and `_REJECTED` (ids only). `ACCOUNT_ROLE_CHANGED` (previous and new role), `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` and `ACCOUNT_REACTIVATED` (ids only). Reasons and notes live in the moderation history instead. Registration numbers, emails and claim messages are never logged. Emails are stored only as a 16-character hash (`emailHash`).

**Finding what happened for a user's error report:**`select * from security_events where metadata->>'requestId' = '<id from the error>';` and search the server logs for `[<id>]`.

## 9. Pending and manual items

1. Apply any deliveries above that are not installed yet, and run `npm install express-rate-limit zod helmet`.
2. **Reset the database password** in Supabase (it was shared in chat and in an uploaded `.env`), then update `DATABASE_URL`.
3. Add `pgbouncer=true` to `DATABASE_URL` (section 6). Keep `DIRECT_URL`: Prisma 6 reads it through `directUrl` in `schema.prisma`.
4. Supabase dashboard: set the minimum password length to 8 (and optionally require letters and numbers).
5. Production: set `CORS_ORIGINS`, `NODE_ENV=production` and `TRUST_PROXY`; configure a custom SMTP provider (Supabase's built-in sender has a low hourly email cap).
6. Convert `prisma/migrations/0_init/migration.sql` from UTF-16 to UTF-8.
7. Clean-up: delete `generated/`, `prisma7.config.ts`, the AI-skill folders, `skills-lock.json` and the diagnostic `test*.js` scripts.
8. Move `superbase-auth-trigger.sql` into a properly named, tracked file, and add a trigger that sets `email_verified_at` when the confirmation link is clicked.
9. Decide a retention period and a scheduled purge for `security_events` and `login_activities` (they hold IP addresses).
10. Not built yet for profiles: avatar upload (an avatar URL is only accepted for files already in this project's Supabase Storage), phone number verification, and the flexible `preferences` / privacy-settings and saved-location fields. Check that the language list in `src/validation/user.schemas.js` matches what the frontend supports.
11. **Clean the imported `hospital_data`:** run the audit queries in section 5, remove spam image links and wrong social-media links. Social links now come only from representatives (task 6c); imported images are still never shown. Suspended hospitals currently stay visible in search (shown as `unclaimed`); say if you would rather hide them.
12. If the hospital table grows well beyond tens of thousands of rows, the typo-tolerant search (which compares every row) and exact text search will need `pg_trgm` GIN indexes; also consider consider PostGIS for near-me search. Current speed with 30,000 test rows: searches 20-200 ms.
13. Review follow-ups: authors are not told when a review is approved or rejected (there is no notifications table yet; they see the status under `GET /api/users/me/reviews`), and there is no way for users to report a review or for hospitals to respond (task 6d).
14. Check that every hospital has a row in `hospital_rating_stats`: `sort=rating` (without near-me) lists hospitals with no row first. In the Supabase SQL editor, `select count(*) from hospitals h left join hospital_rating_stats s on s.hospital_id = h.id where s.hospital_id is null;` should return 0.
15. Commit `prisma/migrations/20261122_add_reviews/migration.sql`; it was missing from the project zip.
16. The roadmap tasks (1 to 7) are all delivered. Not built: push notifications (the `pushNotifications` setting is saved but nothing uses it), bounce handling and delivery tracking, notifying moderators about new claims and reports, appeals for removed reviews and suspensions, flagging reviews before they are reported, visit verification, and user complaints. Paused: age confirmation, onboarding and consent fields. See `PROGRESS.md` for the full list against the PRD.

# Dreel — Hospital Review Platform: Backend

Express 5 API for the Hospital Review Platform (Nigeria first). Authentication is handled by Supabase Auth, data lives in Supabase Postgres, and the app talks to the database through Prisma 6.12.0, which uses its own database engine (there is no `pg` driver adapter and no `pg` package in the app).

> **Keep this README up to date.** Every time a file is added, changed or removed, update this file and the change log at the bottom in the same step.

---

## 1. How this code got here (read this first)

* **Original files** (marked *original* below) came from the backend zip uploaded on 2026-11-21. They were built before the hardening work started.
* **Files marked *added* or *updated*** were created or changed during the hardening work (the database SSL fix and roadmap tasks 1-6b).
* No code has been edited by hand: every change was applied exactly as supplied, so this README describes the current state of the project.
* The files marked *added* or *updated* are what has been **delivered**. Use the install checklist in section 8 to tick off what has been applied, and correct this README if any delivered file has not been applied yet.
